name: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), as published in the Official Journal
aliases: AI Act | Artificial Intelligence Act | Regulation (EU) 2024/1689
description: The EU regulation laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence, dated 13 June 2024 and published in the Official Journal on 12 July 2024. It was later amended; see Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.

document_date_note: The Official Journal header gives 12.7.2024 and the act is dated 13 June 2024 (signature). Records here concern only the AI Act provisions it amends that bear on general-purpose AI model providers.
document_label: As published in the Official Journal (24 July 2026)
document_date_note: The Official Journal header gives 24.7.2026 and the act is dated 8 July 2026 (signature). Article 4 provides entry into force on the third day after publication, which is 27 July 2026; Article 113(d), as inserted, also names 27 July 2026.

name: Estimates of explosive growth within a stated horizon
aliases: Explosive growth estimates within a stated horizon
description: A proposition about the economics of machine intelligence, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code G09, the explosive-growth debate). proposition_criterion: The text states its own estimate of whether or when explosive growth (as the text defines it) occurs in the actual future, with machine intelligence or automation among the stated drivers. Each record gives the holder, the estimate as stated (a number or words), the horizon, the text's definition and the conditions. Records are not converted to a common threshold, combined or ranked; a low estimate and a high estimate both articulate this proposition.

name: Machine substitution for labour produces explosive growth
description: A proposition about the economics of machine intelligence, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code G01, the explosive-growth debate). It is phrased generically and attributed to no one. A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.
proposition_criterion: The text states that if machines (AI systems or emulated minds) can substitute for human labour across all or nearly all tasks, so that labour can be produced like capital, the growth rate of output rises far above historical rates (by roughly an order of magnitude or more) or keeps rising. The conditions under which the text derives this are part of the record.
